newsitem.title: UK: Freight market remains flat, sees grain enquiry.
newsitem.headline: Freight market remains flat, sees grain enquiry.

text.p: The freight market remained very flat today, partly influenced by holidays in the Far East. The BFI gained three points to 1,003 on account of slightly firmer Panamax fixtures in the Pacific.

Some fresh grain enquiry emerged in the Atlantic but so far it has not been translated into higher rates. Some brokers believe that the undertone in the market is healthy but that grain enquiry alone will not be sufficient to make a significant difference to freight levels.

Meanwhile about one third of all Panamaxes now trading are over 15 years of age, considered by brokers to be a remarkably high proportion. Owners of newbuilding Panamaxes are said in a dozen or so cases to be paying for these vessels to be anchored off the yard with a view to deferring delivery until next year.

Panamaxes over 15 years of age are especially vulnerable on the present freight market and vessels such as Evniki (1977) 64,926 dwt are believed to be headed for lay-up in Greece, as well as more modern types such as Waimea (1984) 61,751 dwt.

Some feeble numbers were reported in the grain trades today. Andre paid only $7,500 daily plus $100,000 bonus for Orion II 61,771 dwt delivery Recalada Oct 15/25 for a trip to the Far East, and Egyptian navigation are said to have taken the 1977-built Agia Dynamis 68,598 dwt delivery continent mid Oct for a trip from Northern France to Egyptian Med at about $6,400/6,500 daily.

But a healthy level of fresh enquiry was seen on Tuesday even if charterers rates are still very low. Cargill now has 40-50,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Continent or UK for Oct 14/20 (ideas $8.50), Toepfer 50-55,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Poland for Oct 18/24 (ideas $10.00), Continental 50,000 US Gulf/Aqaba for Oct 8/12, and Dreyfus 50,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Egypt for Oct 11/17 and 55,000 heavy grain US Gulf/China for Oct 21/25.

Glencore were reported to be quoting a Panamax order for Brazil/China for mid-Oct. Chinese Panamax tonnage is rumoured to be available at $18.75 basis no combo for mid-Oct US Gulf/Japan, the same level as last fixed. Cosco has booked Morning Cloud 66,967 dwt on subjects for about 2.5-4.5 months with delivery US Gulf Oct 15/30, possibly at about $7,250 daily plus $100,000 bonus.
In the handies 18-25,000 heavy grain Lakes completing St Lawrence/Venezuela was rumoured fixed and Romac paid only $16.75 for 17,600 wheat from Immingham to two ports Tunisia.

This category is very quiet. Few fixtures have been reported although BHP are understood to have taken modern tonnage for 150,000 ironore Port Hedland/Constanza for Oct/Nov at $7.00, last fixed being Leopardi for 126,000 tonnes at $6.70.

Handy-sizes perhaps the best fixture of the day from owners' point of view was an unnamed fortune type of 22,235 dwt to Brodin delivery prompt Continent for a Lakes round at $6,250 daily. Elsewhere little news emerged although Taxiarhis P 39,000 dwt went for a Petcoke trip from US Gulf to Gibraltar-Hamburg range at only $7,300 daily.
